Definition: Does the government maintain a digital business register?
Comments: Digital business register via Guichet Unique de Création d'Entreprise (GUCE) since 2013; online company registration.
revision_notes: Original sources (investindrc.cd, afrisetup.com) verified and confirm GUCE's role in digital business registration since 2013, with online name-verification and case tracking via e-guce.guichetunique.cd. Cross-checked against the official GUCE portal, the ANAPI procedures page, and a February 2026 World Bank feature confirming GUCE offices are permanently established in only four cities (Kinshasa, Lubumbashi, Kisangani, Goma), with mobile 'caravan' services required in 2025 to extend registration to Bunia, Kananga and Mbuji-Mayi. This corroborates partial rather than full nationwide deployment. Value Code 4 (Partially deployed) confirmed.
revised_comments: The Democratic Republic of Congo maintains a digital business register through the Guichet Unique de Création d'Entreprise (GUCE), operational since 2013 and accessible online via e-guce.guichetunique.cd for company name verification and case tracking. GUCE offices are permanently established in Kinshasa, Lubumbashi, Kisangani and Goma, and the World Bank-supported TRANSFORME project deployed mobile 'caravan' services in 2025 to extend registration access to Bunia, Kananga and Mbuji-Mayi, formalising over 4,600 MSMEs. Coverage remains partial, with many provincial areas still reliant on temporary outreach or the Tribunaux de Commerce rather than permanent digital infrastructure.

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Birth registration completeness ~24.6-40% for children under 5 (2014-2018 data); <20%.
revision_notes: The original Value Code of 1 (<20%) conflicted with its own cited comment, which referenced completeness of 24.6-40% for 2014-2018. Verified UNICEF/World Bank survey data (sourced from DHS/State of the World's Children, via IndexMundi) confirm DRC under-5 birth registration completeness rose from 24.6% (2014 DHS) to 40.1% (2018 DHS). A third DRC DHS was fielded in 2023-24 but its published key-indicators report does not tabulate birth registration, so no more recent country-specific figure could be confirmed by direct reading. UNICEF's December 2024 'Right Start in Life' report puts the Middle Africa subregion (which includes DRC) at 41% under-five birth registration, consistent with the 2018 national figure. On the 20-49% band this corrects Value Code to 2.
revised_comments: Birth registration completeness in the Democratic Republic of Congo stood at around 40% of children under five in the most recent nationally representative survey with published results (2018 DHS), up from 24.6% in 2014. This places coverage within the 20-49% band. UNICEF's regional estimate for Middle Africa, DRC's subregion, puts under-five birth registration at around 41% as of 2024, broadly consistent with the national trend. Coverage remains well below universal registration, reflecting continuing barriers of cost, distance and limited awareness, and a further Demographic and Health Survey conducted in 2023-24 had not yet published birth registration results at the time of writing.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital land register?
Comments: No nationwide digital land register; cadastre digitization planned (e-Foncier project signed 2022 with eProseed). Mining cadastre digital exists.
revision_notes: Original sources (wearetech.africa, drclicences.cami.cd) verified; the mining cadastre portal is a separate system from the general land title register and does not itself establish a digital land register. Fresh reporting confirms the original 2022 e-Foncier contract with Luxembourg firm eProseed collapsed by early 2025 ('l'échec du contrat signé avec... eProseed en 2022'), after which the government engaged a new partner, Dubai-based Oxinus, to relaunch a blockchain-based e-Foncier platform. A pilot blockchain land-management project with Duna RWA launched in June 2025, and a major land law reform (Law n°25/62, promulgated December 2025/January 2026) mandates full digitisation of the cadastre. No nationwide digital land register is yet operational, so Value Code 3 (Under development) remains the accurate assessment, now grounded in more current evidence than the original 2022 source.
revised_comments: The Democratic Republic of Congo does not yet maintain an operational nationwide digital land register. Following the collapse of a 2022 contract with Luxembourg firm eProseed, the government partnered with Dubai-based Oxinus in early 2025 to relaunch the e-Foncier digitisation programme, and piloted a blockchain-based land title system with Duna RWA from June 2025. A major land law reform (Law n°25/62 of December 2025), the first substantive revision of land legislation since 1973, mandates full digitisation of the cadastre and modernised land administration, but implementation across the country's 26 provinces remains at an early stage. A separate digital mining cadastre operates independently of the general land title register.
